items.title: Component amplitudes, coherent and incoherent bin laws, and recorded detector weights
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited Hilbert-space and measure suppliers. Let
$(D,\mathcal A,dx)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space ([[def-measure]]), let
$r\ge1$ be an integer, and let
$$L^{2}(D;\mathbb C^{r}):=\Bigl\{f:D\to\mathbb C^{r}\ \text{measurable}:\ \int_{D}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx<\infty\Bigr\}\Big/\!\sim,$$
the quotient by equality $dx$-almost everywhere
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]), with
$$\langle f,g\rangle:=\int_{D}\langle f(x),g(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}\,dx,\qquad \|f\|^{2}:=\langle f,f\rangle=\int_{D}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx,$$
linear in the first argument ([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]).
For $a,b\in L^{2}(D;\mathbb C^{r})$ and measurable $B\subseteq D$ write
$$\langle a,b\rangle_{B}:=\int_{B}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}\,dx,\qquad N:=\|a\|^{2}+\|b\|^{2},\qquad c:=\operatorname{Re}\langle a,b\rangle_{D}.$$
Then:

(a) *Pointwise and integrated cross term.* For $dx$-almost every $x\in D$,
$$\|a(x)+b(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}=\|a(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|b(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+2\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}},$$
and for every measurable $B\subseteq D$, the three functions $\|a\|^{2}$,
$\|b\|^{2}$, $\langle a,b\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}$ being $dx$-integrable on $B$,
$$\int_{B}\|a+b\|^{2}\,dx=\int_{B}\|a\|^{2}\,dx+\int_{B}\|b\|^{2}\,dx+2\operatorname{Re}\langle a,b\rangle_{B}.$$

(b) *Coherent bin law.* If $\|a+b\|>0$, then
$$p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B):=\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|a+b\|^{2}\,dx}{\|a+b\|^{2}}\qquad(B\in\mathcal A)$$
defines a probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$
([[def-probability-measure]]), and for every $B\in\mathcal A$ the expansion of
(a) holds with $\|a+b\|^{2}=N+2c$ in the denominator.

(c) *Incoherent bin law.* If $\|a\|>0$, $\|b\|>0$ and $w\in[0,1]$, then
$$p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B):=w\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|a\|^{2}\,dx}{\|a\|^{2}}+(1-w)\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|b\|^{2}\,dx}{\|b\|^{2}}\qquad(B\in\mathcal A)$$
defines a probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$.

(d) *Recorded weights, sub-probability and conditioning.* Let $\mu$ be a
probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$ and let $W:D\to[0,1]$ be measurable.
Then $B\mapsto\nu(B):=\int_{B}W\,d\mu$ is a finite measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$
with $0\le\nu(D)\le1$; if $\nu(D)>0$, then
$\bar\nu(B):=\nu(B)/\nu(D)$ defines a probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$.
More generally, for finitely many measurable weights $W_{1},\dots,W_{m}:D\to[0,1]$
with $\sum_{a=1}^{m}W_{a}\le1$ pointwise, the numbers
$\nu_{a}:=\int_{D}W_{a}\,d\mu$ satisfy $\nu_{a}\ge0$ and
$\sum_{a=1}^{m}\nu_{a}\le1$; if $\sum_{a=1}^{m}W_{a}=1$ pointwise, then
$\sum_{a=1}^{m}\nu_{a}=1$.

(e) *Coincidence criterion.* Let $\|a\|>0$, $\|b\|>0$ and put
$w_{*}:=\|a\|^{2}/N$, so that $p_{\mathrm{mix}}$ with weight $w_{*}$ is
$p_{*}(B)=N^{-1}\int_{B}\bigl(\|a\|^{2}+\|b\|^{2}\bigr)dx$. Then
$p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B)=p_{*}(B)$ for every $B\in\mathcal A$ if and only if
$$N\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=c\,\bigl(\|a(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|b(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\bigr)\qquad\text{for }dx\text{-almost every }x\in D .$$
In particular, if $\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for almost every
$x$, then the two laws coincide; and if $c=0$, then they coincide if and only
if $\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for almost
every $x$.

The assertions concern the specified classes and weights only; no probability
law of an apparatus, no sample of trials and no empirical claim is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice; a $\sigma$-finite measure space $(D,\mathcal A,dx)$; an integer $r\ge1$; classes $a,b\in L^{2}(D;\mathbb C^{r})$; a probability measure $\mu$ on $(D,\mathcal A)$; measurable weights $W,W_{1},\dots,W_{m}:D\to[0,1]$; reals $w\in[0,1]$.

[F1] **Componentwise $L^{2}$ and its pairing.** For $f=(f_{1},\dots,f_{r})$ with components in the scalar space $L^{2}(D;\mathbb C)$ of [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]], the integral $\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\int_{D}f_{l}\overline{g_{l}}\,dx$ is finite and defines an inner product, linear in the first argument, with $\|f\|^{2}=\sum_{l}\|f_{l}\|^{2}$; for every measurable $B$ the partial pairing satisfies $|\langle f,g\rangle_{B}|\le\|f\|_{L^{2}(B)}\|g\|_{L^{2}(B)}\le\|f\|\,\|g\|$ ([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]], [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]], [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]]). Two choices of representatives of $f,g$ change $x\mapsto\langle f(x),g(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}$ and $x\mapsto\|f(x)+g(x)\|^{2}$ only on a $dx$-null set, so the pointwise assertions are well posed almost everywhere.

[F2] **Indefinite integrals are measures.** For nonnegative measurable $h$ the set function $B\mapsto\int_{B}h\,dx$ is a measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$ ([[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]]); for $g\in L^{1}(dx)$ the real and imaginary parts of $B\mapsto\int_{B}g\,dx$ are countably additive by monotone convergence ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]).

[F3] **Monotonicity of the integral.** If $0\le h\le H$ are measurable, then $\int_{D}h\,dx\le\int_{D}H\,dx$ ([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]).

[F4] **Probability measures and normalization.** A probability measure is a measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$ with total mass $1$ ([[def-probability-measure]], [[def-measure]]). A finite measure $\nu\ge0$ with $0<\nu(D)<\infty$ is normalized to a probability measure by $\bar\nu(B)=\nu(B)/\nu(D)$, because countable additivity divided by the constant $\nu(D)$ stays countably additive and $\bar\nu(D)=1$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; expand the squared component norm pointwise, then read off in turn the two normalized laws and the weight bounds, integrate the cross term, normalize it, and compute the coincidence condition from the two displayed formulas.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Pointwise identity] Fix representatives of $a,b$. For every $x\in D$ the identity $\|a(x)+b(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}=\|a(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|b(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+2\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}$ holds by the expansion of the finite-dimensional inner product; by [F1] the three real functions $x\mapsto\|a(x)\|^{2}$, $\|b(x)\|^{2}$ and $\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle$ are measurable, and the last is integrable because $|\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle|\le\|a(x)\|\,\|b(x)\|$ with $\|a\|\,\|b\|\in L^{1}(dx)$; representatives differing on null sets change the identity only on a null set. This proves the pointwise assertion of (a). [given, F1, algebra]

1.2 [Incoherent law] Assume $\|a\|,\|b\|>0$. By [F2] each of $B\mapsto\int_{B}\|a\|^{2}dx$ and $B\mapsto\int_{B}\|b\|^{2}dx$ is a finite measure with positive total masses $\|a\|^{2}$ and $\|b\|^{2}$; by [F4] each normalized set function is a probability measure, and a convex combination with $w\in[0,1]$ of two probability measures is again a probability measure, because countable additivity is preserved and $w\cdot1+(1-w)\cdot1=1$. This is (c). [F2, F4, algebra]

1.3 [Recorded weights] Applying [F3] with $h=W$ and $H=1$ gives $\nu(D)=\int_{D}W\,d\mu\le\int_{D}1\,d\mu=1$ and $\nu(B)\ge0$ for every $B$ because $W\ge0$; countable additivity of $\nu$ follows from [F2] applied to the measure $\mu$. If $\nu(D)>0$, [F4] makes $\bar\nu$ a probability measure. For the finite family, $\nu_{a}=\int_{D}W_{a}d\mu\ge0$ and $\sum_{a}\nu_{a}=\int_{D}\sum_{a}W_{a}\,d\mu\le\int_{D}1\,d\mu=1$ by finite additivity and [F3]; if $\sum_{a}W_{a}=1$ pointwise, the middle integral equals $\mu(D)=1$. This is (d). [F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Integrated identity] Let $B\in\mathcal A$. Integrating the identity of step 1.1 over $B$ is legitimate because all three terms are integrable on $B$ by step 1.1 and [F1]; the integral of the left side is $\int_{B}\|a+b\|^{2}dx$ and the integral of the right side is $\int_{B}\|a\|^{2}dx+\int_{B}\|b\|^{2}dx+2\operatorname{Re}\langle a,b\rangle_{B}$, which is the displayed identity of (a). [step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 [Coherent law] Assume $\|a+b\|>0$. The set function $B\mapsto\int_{B}\|a+b\|^{2}dx$ is a finite measure with total mass $\|a+b\|^{2}$ by [F2], and $\|a+b\|^{2}\in(0,\infty)$; dividing by this constant gives a finite measure of total mass one, hence a probability measure by [F4], whose value at $B$ is $p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B)$ with denominator $N+2c$ by step 2.1 applied to $B=D$. This is (b). [step 2.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Coincidence criterion] By steps 2.1 and 1.2 with $w=w_{*}$, $p_{*}(B)=\frac{1}{N}\int_{B}(\|a\|^{2}+\|b\|^{2})dx$ and $p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B)=\frac{\int_{B}(\|a\|^{2}+\|b\|^{2})dx+2c(B)}{N+2c}$ with $c(B):=\operatorname{Re}\langle a,b\rangle_{B}$; since $N>0$ and $N+2c=\|a+b\|^{2}>0$, the equality $p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B)=p_{*}(B)$ is equivalent to $N c(B)=c\,M(B)$ for the finite measure $M(B):=\int_{B}(\|a\|^{2}+\|b\|^{2})dx$. The signed measure $N c(\cdot)-c\,M(\cdot)$ vanishes on every $B\in\mathcal A$ if and only if its density $N\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}-c(\|a(x)\|^{2}+\|b(x)\|^{2})$ vanishes $dx$-almost everywhere by [F2], since a nonzero integrable density has a level set of strictly positive or strictly negative integral. This is the displayed criterion; if $\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle=0$ a.e., then $c=0$ and $c(B)=0$ for every $B$, so the laws coincide, and if $c=0$ the criterion reduces to $\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle=0$ a.e. This proves (e), and steps 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.1, 3.1 prove the remaining clauses. [step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1, step 3.1, F1, F2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Convention.** The pairing is linear in the first argument, as fixed by the cited $L^{2}$ items, so the cross term of a sum $a+b$ is $2\operatorname{Re}\langle a,b\rangle$ and not $2\operatorname{Re}\langle b,a\rangle$; the two agree because the real part is symmetric.
- **What is not asserted.** The lemma is an identity and inequality package for classes and weights; it produces no detector law, no state update, no sample of trials and no measured frequency. The coincidence criterion concerns the two declared laws, not the question of which preparation a laboratory realizes.

items.title: The declared two-path preparation model and its ideal detection bins
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the kinematics and one-particle model
postulate P5, the identical-particle and spin postulate P6, and the preparation
and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a spin label
$s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $r:=2s+1$, and fix a mass parameter
$m>0$. The state space is $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ of
almost-everywhere classes with the pairing linear in the first argument
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). The position assignment is
the model's componentwise position family $Q_{1},Q_{2},Q_{3}$, whose joint
spectral projection-valued measure is $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$ on the Borel
sets of $\mathbb R^{3}$ and whose outcome law in a pure preparation of the unit
vector $\psi$ is
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$$
([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b),
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b));
the unit read from $G$ is the position unit of the model's quantity
conventions, the metre, and the outcome sets $B$ are read as subsets of
$\mathbb R^{3}$ ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]). Assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the
cited suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Declared two-path assignment.** A **declared two-path preparation model**
of the apparatus is the assignment of two nonzero classes
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, called the **path components** of the model with
respect to the declared pair of alternative path conditions of the apparatus,
together with a declared **relative phase** $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ and a declared
**weight** $w\in[0,1]$. The assignment of $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}$, $\varphi$ and
$w$ is part of the preparation model in the sense of clause (i) of P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]): it is declared, not
computed from the framework, and no item of this page asserts that a particle
described by the model "took" one of the two paths.

**(c) Coherent preparation.** The declared two-path model is **admissible at
phase $\varphi$** when $\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\ne0$ in $H_{s}$. When it
is admissible, the **coherent preparation** of relative phase $\varphi$ is the
pure preparation
$$\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi):=\widehat\rho\bigl(\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\bigr),$$
the normalized rank-one operator of the nonzero vector
$\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). It is a state of
the model, and the relative phase $\varphi$ is read in radians (dimensionless);
a common phase of $\psi_{1}$ and $\psi_{2}$ is immaterial because it acts on
the vector $\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}$ as a global phase
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]).

**(d) Incoherent preparation.** For a declared weight $w\in[0,1]$ the
**incoherent preparation**, or **which-path preparation**, of the model is
$$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w):=w\,\widehat\rho(\psi_{1})+(1-w)\,\widehat\rho(\psi_{2}).$$
It is a state of the model: the normalized rank-one operators are states, and
$D(H_{s})$ is closed under finite real convex combinations
([[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-density-set-convex-and-complete]] clause (a),
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). The weight $w$ is a
declared preparation weight, not an outcome probability.

**(e) Ideal detection bins.** A **declared ideal detector** of the model is a
finite family $\mathcal B=(B_{a})_{a=1}^{m}$ of pairwise disjoint Borel subsets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with $\bigcup_{a}B_{a}=\mathbb R^{3}$; the **ideal bin
probabilities** of a preparation $\rho\in D(H_{s})$ are the numbers
$$p_{a}(\rho):=\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B_{a})=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,G(B_{a})\bigr)\qquad(a=1,\dots,m),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2 for the joint position assignment
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)). By
clause (b) of P2 these numbers are nonnegative, are at most one, and satisfy
$\sum_{a}p_{a}(\rho)=1$. A single **declared bin** $B$ is the two-element ideal
detector $(B,\mathbb R^{3}\setminus B)$; its probability is $\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B)$.
The positive Borel set $\{x:\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}>0\}$ of a pure
preparation with unit vector $\psi$ is its **ideal support**, read only almost
everywhere.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model data of the pair:
the framework reading, the declared path components and preparations, and the
ideal bin reading of the position observable. They adopt no assumption beyond
P1, P2, P5, P6, P7 and the cited mathematics; the declaration of
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\varphi,w$ and of the bins is an apparatus-model input, and
the claim that a concrete two-slit apparatus realizes a particular such
declaration is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7(iii). The
declared bins are subsets of $\mathbb R^{3}$; the model does not claim that a
physical screen of lower dimension is literally a spatial region, and a
marginal, coarse-graining or flux reduction of a state to a screen coordinate
or surface is a separate detection model, not supplied here. No dynamics, no
recorded-event response, no sampling model and no empirical result is
asserted; the recorded-event and sampling models are declared separately on
this page.

## Remarks

- **Classes, not functions.** The path components are almost-everywhere
  classes; pointwise values such as $\psi_{j}(x)$ are read only through the
  densities and pairings of the cited items, and the interference identities of
  the page hold up to null sets.
- **"Path" is a declared decomposition.** The phrase "path component" names an
  element of the declared decomposition of the preparation model. The pair
  proves laws of the declared coherent and incoherent preparations; it does not
  assert which-path ontology, does not assign a trajectory to the particle, and
  does not assume that the two components are orthogonal or have disjoint ideal
  supports. Whether a preparation model with an orthogonal or disjoint-support
  decomposition describes a given apparatus is a physical identification under
  P7.
- **Units.** The outcome sets are sets of position with unit metre, the
  probability numbers are dimensionless, and the phase is read in radians
  ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]).

items.physical_scope: A declared preparation and detection model for a two-path interference arrangement in the massive spin-s model of the framework: two declared nonzero path-component classes of the model state space, the coherent preparations of a declared relative phase, the declared incoherent (which-path) preparations with declared weights, and the ideal detection-bin reading of the model's joint position observable. The model is a declaration of the apparatus and preparation assignment in the sense of the preparation and apparatus postulate P7; it asserts no derivation of the path decomposition from the framework, no claim that any particle took a definite path, no detector response or sampling model, no experiment and no empirical result. Spatial bins are regions of R^3; a lower-dimensional material screen and any marginal or flux reduction of a state to it are separate models, not claimed here.

items.title: The declared recorded detector and sampling model of the two-path arrangement
items.statement:
## Definition

Adopt the declared two-path preparation model of
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], the
unsharp finite-outcome clause (iv) of the observable and probability postulate
P2, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). The following vocabulary is used
by this page.

**(a) Declared recorded detector.** A **declared recorded detector** of the
arrangement is a finite set $A$ of **recorded outcome labels**, together with
measurable **recorded weights** $w_{a}:\mathbb R^{3}\to[0,1]$ for $a\in A$ such
that $\sum_{a\in A}w_{a}(x)\le1$ for almost every $x\in\mathbb R^{3}$. The
**effect** of the label $a$ is the multiplication operator
$$F_{a}:=M_{w_{a}},\qquad (M_{w}\psi)(x):=w(x)\psi(x),$$
on $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, and the **no-record effect** is
$$F_{0}:=I-\sum_{a\in A}F_{a}.$$
Each $F_{a}$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) with $0\le F_{a}\le I$ in the
quadratic-form order, and $\sum_{a\in A}F_{a}+F_{0}=I$ with $0\le F_{0}\le I$:
multiplication by a measurable weight $0\le w\le1$ is bounded with
$\|M_{w}\|\le1$ by [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], self-adjoint by
[[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], and nonnegative with $M_{w}\le I$ by the order
of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]; the sum
$F_{0}=M_{1-\sum_{a}w_{a}}$ is of the same form because $0\le1-\sum_{a}w_{a}\le1$.
Thus $(F_{a})_{a\in A}\cup\{F_{0}\}$ is a finite family of bounded effects
with nonnegative terms summing to the identity, of the kind of clause (iv) of
P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).

**(b) Recorded probabilities.** For a preparation $\rho\in D(H_{s})$ the
**recorded probability** of a label $a\in A$ and the **no-record probability**
are
$$\nu(a):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho F_{a}\bigr),\qquad \nu(0):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho F_{0}\bigr)=1-\sum_{a\in A}\nu(a),$$
the outcome reading of clause (iv) of P2 for the declared effects
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (f)
records the reading; the numbers are nonnegative and sum to one). The
**recorded-event mass** is $\nu(A):=\sum_{a\in A}\nu(a)=1-\nu(0)\in[0,1]$. A
detector is **full-efficiency** when $\sum_{a}w_{a}=1$ almost everywhere, so
that $F_{0}=0$ and $\nu(0)=0$; otherwise the model **loses** events, and the
no-record channel carries the lost mass. A **declared recorded bin** $B$ is
the special case with one label $a$ and $w_{a}=\mathbf 1_{B}$; then
$F_{a}=G(B)$ is the position projection of clause (e) of
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], with the
position set $B$ read in the metre unit of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and the recorded probability is
the ideal bin probability.

**(c) Loss conditioning.** When $\nu(A)>0$, the **conditioned recorded law** is
$$\bar\nu(a):=\frac{\nu(a)}{\nu(A)}\qquad(a\in A).$$
It is a probability measure on the finite set $A$
([[def-probability-measure]]); it is the law of the recorded label under the
declared model conditioned on the occurrence of a record. Conditioning is a
statistical operation on the recorded data; it is not a state update, and no
claim of P3 is made here.

**(d) Sampling model.** A **declared $N$-trial sampling model** for a fixed
preparation $\rho$ is a probability space carrying random elements
$O_{1},\dots,O_{N}:\Omega\to A\cup\{0\}$ ($N\ge1$), where $0$ is the no-record
label of clause (b), that are **mutually independent** in the sense of
[[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]] and **identically distributed**
with $\mathbb P(O_{k}=a)=\nu(a)$ for every $a\in A$, $\mathbb P(O_{k}=0)=\nu(0)$
and every $k$, where $\nu$ is the recorded law of clause (b); the numbers
$\nu(a)$ and $\nu(0)$ sum to one, so this is a probability law on the finite
set $A\cup\{0\}$. The **empirical frequency** of the label $a$ in the sample is
$$F_{N}(a):=\frac{1}{N}\#\{k:O_{k}=a\}.$$
A **declared fringe criterion** for sample size $N$ is a subset
$C\subseteq(A\cup\{0\})^{N}$; the model **accepts** the sample when
$(O_{1},\dots,O_{N})\in C$ and **fails the criterion** otherwise. The
identification of repetitions of a concrete procedure with the independent
identically distributed model is an additional statistical assumption in the
sense of clause (ii) of P7; it is not a consequence of P1-P6, and correlated
trials, drifting preparation, dead time and selection must be modeled or
recorded as limitations if present ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix the recorded-detector and sampling
vocabulary of the pair and read clause (iv) of P2 and clauses (i)-(iii) of P7.
The recorded weights, the label set, the conditioning convention and the
sampling model are declared apparatus and procedure inputs. The claim "this
apparatus realizes the effect family $F_{a}$" and the claim "its repetitions
are independent and identically distributed draws of $\nu$" are physical
identifications with uncertainty under P7(iii) and P7(ii), can fail, and are
not derived here. No calibration, efficiency, background or resolution value
is asserted, no counts are recorded, and no statistical-inference conclusion
is drawn by this definition.

## Remarks

- **Relations between the detector families.** The ideal detector of clause
  (e) of [[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] is
  the full-efficiency case $w_{a}=\mathbf 1_{B_{a}}$ of a declared recorded
  detector whose labels partition the bin family; a general recorded detector
  with non-indicator weights represents finite resolution, response and
  efficiency through its weights, and its no-record channel represents lost
  events.
- **No state update is declared.** The item declares outcome probabilities
  only. Which post-measurement state, if any, a registration leaves behind is a
  separate instrument-model question and is not part of this page.

The item asserts no detector realization, no calibration, no measured counts and no statistical-inference conclusion; the recorded-event probabilities are read from the declared effects, and the identification of a concrete apparatus with these effects and of its repetitions with the sampling model is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.

items.title: Coherent and which-path detection laws of the declared two-path model
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor
postulate P6 as read by
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], and the
preparation and apparatus discipline P7, and adopt the declared two-path
preparation model of that definition with path components
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, relative phase
$\varphi\in\mathbb R$ and weight $w\in[0,1]$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Write $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$ for the joint
position projection-valued measure of the model,
$\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho G(B))$ for its outcome law
([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b)), and put
$$N:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2},\qquad c(B):=\operatorname{Re}\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx,\qquad c:=c(\mathbb R^{3}).$$
Then:

(a) *Coherent law.* If the declared model is admissible at phase $\varphi$,
then for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)}(B)=\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}(x)+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}} ,$$
and the numerator expands as
$$\int_{B}\bigl(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}\bigr)dx+2\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(e^{-i\varphi}\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx\Bigr),$$
with denominator $N+2\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}c)$; in particular
$\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}>0$.

(b) *Which-path law.* For the declared weight $w\in[0,1]$ and every Borel set
$B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$,
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)}(B)=w\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}}+(1-w)\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}} .$$

(c) *Coincidence criterion.* Let $w_{*}:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}/N$, so that
$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w_{*})}(B)=N^{-1}\int_{B}(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})dx$.
Then $\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(0)}(B)=\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w_{*})}(B)$
for every Borel set $B$ if and only if
$$N\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=c\,\bigl(\|\psi_{1}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\bigr)\qquad\text{for almost every }x .$$
In particular, if $\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for
almost every $x$, then the coherent law of phase $0$ and the which-path law of
weight $w_{*}$ agree on every bin; and if $c=0$, then they agree if and only if
$\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for
almost every $x$.

(d) *Scope.* Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional on P1, P2, P5, P6 and the
declared model, and identify the laws of exactly two declared preparations.
They assert no path ontology, use no entangled marker state and no reduced
state, assert no detector response, no loss, no sampling model, no dynamics and
no empirical result.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1, P2, P5, P6 and P7 read through the cited items; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the declared model data $\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\varphi,w$ with $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\ne0$ and, where claimed, $\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\ne0$; Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$.

[F1] **Position law of the model.** For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ the joint position law of the model is $\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}dx$, a probability measure on the Borel sets, and it depends only on the ray $[\psi]$ ([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clauses (b) and (e), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).

[F2] **Outcome law and affinity.** The outcome law of a preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$, it is affine in the preparation, and a finite real convex combination of states is a state ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]], [[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] clause (d)).

[F3] **Declared preparations.** The coherent preparation is the pure preparation of the nonzero vector $\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}$, and the which-path preparation is $w\widehat\rho(\psi_{1})+(1-w)\widehat\rho(\psi_{2})$ ([[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] clauses (c) and (d)).

[F4] **Inner-product and law package.** For $a,b\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ the pointwise identity $\|a+b\|^{2}=\|a\|^{2}+\|b\|^{2}+2\operatorname{Re}\langle a,b\rangle$ holds almost everywhere and integrally over every Borel set, the coherent law $p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B)=\|a+b\|^{-2}\int_{B}\|a+b\|^{2}dx$ and the incoherent law with norm weights are probability measures, and the coincidence criterion of [[lem-nrqm-interference-component-cross-term-and-recorded-bin-laws]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (e) holds; the pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; apply the model's position law to the declared coherent and which-path preparations, use affinity for the mixture, expand the cross term with the math lemma and read off the coincidence criterion.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Coherent law] Assume admissibility. Put $u:=(\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2})/\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|$, a unit vector, so that $\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)=\widehat\rho(u)$ by [F3]. [F1] gives $\mu^{G}_{u}(B)=\int_{B}\|u(x)\|^{2}dx$; substituting $u$ and using $\|u\|=1$ gives the formula of (a) for the law and the identity $\|u(x)\|^{2}=\|\psi_{1}(x)+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}(x)\|^{2}/\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}$. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

1.2 [Which-path law] By [F2] and [F3], $\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)}(B)=w\,\mu^{G}_{\widehat\rho(\psi_{1})}(B)+(1-w)\,\mu^{G}_{\widehat\rho(\psi_{2})}(B)$; applying [F1] to the normalized vectors $\psi_{1}/\|\psi_{1}\|$ and $\psi_{2}/\|\psi_{2}\|$ gives $\mu^{G}_{\widehat\rho(\psi_{j})}(B)=\int_{B}\|\psi_{j}\|^{2}dx/\|\psi_{j}\|^{2}$ for $j=1,2$, which is (b). [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.3 [Cross-term expansion] Apply [F4] with $a=\psi_{1}$ and $b=e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}$: $\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}dx=\int_{B}(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})dx+2\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1},e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\rangle_{B}$; by conjugate-linearity in the second argument, $\langle\psi_{1},e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\rangle_{B}=e^{-i\varphi}\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx$, and at $B=\mathbb R^{3}$ the denominator is $N+2\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}c)$ with $N>0$, so it is positive. This is the expansion of (a). [given, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Coincidence criterion] Apply [F4] to $a=\psi_{1}$, $b=\psi_{2}$: the criterion of the math lemma states that $p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B)=p_{*}(B)$ for every Borel $B$ with $p_{*}(B)=N^{-1}\int_{B}(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})dx$ if and only if the displayed almost-everywhere relation holds. By step 1.1 with $\varphi=0$ the framework coherent law equals $p_{\mathrm{coh}}$, and by step 1.2 with $w=w_{*}$ the framework which-path law equals $p_{*}$; the criterion therefore transfers to the framework laws, and the two special cases follow from the same relation. This proves (c), and steps 1.1-1.3 prove (a) and (b); clause (d) records the scope. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, F2, F4, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **The cross term is physical relative phase.** A change of the relative phase
  $\varphi$ rotates the cross term $e^{-i\varphi}c(B)$ without changing the two
  path densities; a common phase of $\psi_{1}$ and $\psi_{2}$ is immaterial.
- **What the theorem does not claim.** It does not assert that the coherent
  preparation is "more correct" than the which-path preparation, that a
  particle took a particular path, or that any apparatus realizes either
  declaration; and it makes no claim about visibility loss by entanglement or
  path marking, which belongs to the entanglement model of the category.

The statement is a conditional consequence of the state and observable postulates P1 and P2, the model postulates P5 and P6, the declared apparatus and preparation assignment in the sense of P7, and the cited mathematics. It asserts no which-path ontology, no entanglement or marker interaction, no detector response, no dynamics and no empirical result; the coherent and the which-path law are properties of two declared preparation models, and the identification of a concrete arrangement with either model is a tested identification with uncertainty.

items.title: Recorded bin laws, loss and conditioning of the declared two-path detector
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 in its unsharp finite-outcome
reading, the declared two-path preparation model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] with path
components $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\ne0$, relative phase $\varphi$ and weight $w$, and
the declared recorded detector
[[def-nrqm-interference-recorded-detector-and-sampling-model]] with finite
label set $A$, recorded weights $w_{a}$ and effects $F_{a}=M_{w_{a}}$, no-record
effect $F_{0}=I-\sum_{a}F_{a}$, recorded probabilities $\nu(a)$ and recorded-event
mass $\nu(A)=\sum_{a\in A}\nu(a)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited trace-class,
rank-one and square-root suppliers. Let
$\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)$ be the declared
coherent and which-path preparations and put $N:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}$,
$c:=\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle$ and
$w_{*}:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}/N$. Then:

(a) *Recorded coherent law.* If the model is admissible at phase $\varphi$,
then for every label $a\in A$
$$\nu_{\mathrm{coh}(\varphi)}(a)=\frac{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}(x)\,\|\psi_{1}(x)+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}} ,$$
and the numerator equals
$$\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}\bigl(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}\bigr)dx+2\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(e^{-i\varphi}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx\Bigr).$$

(b) *Recorded which-path law.* For the declared weight $w\in[0,1]$ and every
$a\in A$,
$$\nu_{\mathrm{mix}(w)}(a)=w\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}dx}{\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}}+(1-w)\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}dx}{\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}} .$$

(c) *Loss.* The no-record probability is
$\nu(0)=1-\nu(A)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{0})\ge0$, so $\nu(A)\le1$. If
$\sum_{a}w_{a}=1$ almost everywhere, then $F_{0}=0$ and $\nu(0)=0$ for every
preparation; if $F_{0}\ne0$, then there is a declared pure preparation with
$\nu(0)>0$. When $\nu(A)>0$, the conditioned recorded law
$\bar\nu(a)=\nu(a)/\nu(A)$ is a probability measure on $A$.

(d) *Ideal bins and coincidence.* If $w_{a}=\mathbf 1_{B_{a}}$ for a declared
ideal detector $(B_{a})_{a=1}^{m}$, then
$\nu(a)=\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B_{a})$ is the ideal bin probability of
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]]. Moreover, if
the almost-everywhere relation
$$N\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=c\,\bigl(\|\psi_{1}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\bigr)$$
of clause (c) of that theorem holds, then the recorded coherent law of phase
$0$ and the recorded which-path law of weight $w_{*}$ agree, $\nu_{\mathrm{coh}(0)}(a)=\nu_{\mathrm{mix}(w_{*})}(a)$,
for every label $a$ of every declared recorded detector.

(e) *Scope.* Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional on P2, the declared preparation
and detector models and the cited mathematics; they assert no calibration, no
resolution, background or efficiency value, no state update, no counts and no
empirical result, and the claim that a concrete apparatus realizes the declared
effects is a tested identification with uncertainty.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates and declared models read as in the statement; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; labels $a\in A$; preparations $\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)$; weights $w_{a}$ and effects $F_{a}=M_{w_{a}}$, $F_{0}=I-\sum_{a}F_{a}$; the constants $N,c,w_{*}$.

[F1] **Unsharp finite outcomes.** Clause (iv) of P2 states that a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels is described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of bounded operators with $0\le F_{a}\le I$ in the quadratic-form order and $\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$, the outcome probabilities being $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})\ge0$ with $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] clause (iv)).

[F2] **Declared recorded detector.** The recorded weights $w_{a}$ are measurable $[0,1]$-valued with $\sum_{a}w_{a}\le1$ almost everywhere, the effects are $F_{a}=M_{w_{a}}$ and $F_{0}=I-\sum_{a}F_{a}$ with $0\le F_{a},F_{0}\le I$ and $\sum_{a}F_{a}+F_{0}=I$, the recorded probabilities are $\nu(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ and $\nu(0)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{0})=1-\sum_{a}\nu(a)$, the recorded-event mass is $\nu(A)=\sum_{a}\nu(a)$, and the conditioned recorded law is $\bar\nu(a)=\nu(a)/\nu(A)$ when $\nu(A)>0$ ([[def-nrqm-interference-recorded-detector-and-sampling-model]] clauses (a)-(c)). In particular $\sum_{a}w_{a}=1$ almost everywhere exactly when $F_{0}=0$.

[F3] **Rank-one pairing.** For $u,v$ in a complex Hilbert space, $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ is trace class with $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$, and for bounded $B$ one has $T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B^{*}v}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (b) and (d)).

[F4] **Trace calculus.** The trace is linear in its trace-class variable and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal, so $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(F+G))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F)+\operatorname{tr}(\rho G)$ for a preparation $\rho$ and bounded $F,G$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]], [[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]).

[F5] **Weighted bin laws.** For $a,b\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ and measurable $0\le W\le1$ one has $\int W\|a+b\|^{2}dx=\int W(\|a\|^{2}+\|b\|^{2})dx+2\operatorname{Re}\int W\langle a,b\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx$ by the pointwise and integrated cross-term identity of [[lem-nrqm-interference-component-cross-term-and-recorded-bin-laws]] clause (a); and for a probability measure $\mu$ and weights $0\le W_{a}\le1$ with $\sum_{a}W_{a}\le1$ the numbers $\int W_{a}d\mu$ are nonnegative with sum at most one, the conditioning statement holding when the sum is positive ([[lem-nrqm-interference-component-cross-term-and-recorded-bin-laws]] clause (d)).

[F6] **Declared preparation laws.** For the declared preparations, $\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)}(B)=\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{-2}\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}dx$ and $\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)}(B)=w\|\psi_{1}\|^{-2}\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}dx+(1-w)\|\psi_{2}\|^{-2}\int_{B}\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}dx$; the ideal bin probability is $\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B_{a})$ and the coincidence relation displayed in the statement holds exactly when the coherent law of phase $0$ and the which-path law of weight $w_{*}$ agree on every bin ([[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F7] **Positive square root.** Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every bounded positive operator $T$ on a nonzero complex Hilbert space has a bounded positive square root $T^{1/2}$ with $T^{1/2}T^{1/2}=T$; if $Tx\ne0$ then $T^{1/2}x\ne0$, so $\langle Tx,x\rangle=\|T^{1/2}x\|^{2}>0$ ([[thm-positive-square-root]]).

[F8] **Probability measures on a finite set.** A probability measure on a $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal A$ is a measure with total mass one ([[def-probability-measure]], [[def-measure]]); on a finite set with the $\sigma$-algebra of all subsets, a nonnegative function of the atoms whose values sum to one extends uniquely to a probability measure, because finite additivity is read off the atoms and every countably disjoint family has only finitely many nonempty members.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the trace pairing of a pure preparation with a multiplication effect, substitute the declared preparations and use trace linearity for the mixture, read loss off the completed effect family, and expand the weighted cross term to transfer the coincidence relation.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [Pure-state pairing] Let $\psi\ne0$ and let $W$ be a measurable $[0,1]$-valued weight with effect $M_{W}$. Since the normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$ is $\widehat\rho(\psi)=T_{\psi,\psi}/\|\psi\|^{2}$, [F3] with $B=M_{W}$ gives $T_{\psi,\psi}M_{W}=T_{\psi,M_{W}\psi}$ (the effect is self-adjoint), so $\operatorname{tr}(\widehat\rho(\psi)M_{W})=\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,M_{W}\psi})/\|\psi\|^{2}=\langle\psi,M_{W}\psi\rangle/\|\psi\|^{2}=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}W\|\psi\|^{2}dx/\|\psi\|^{2}$. [given, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Recorded laws] For the coherent preparation, [F2] and step 1.1 with $\psi=\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}$ and $W=w_{a}$ give $\nu_{\mathrm{coh}(\varphi)}(a)=\int w_{a}\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}dx/\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}$; substituting the weighted identity of [F5] gives the stated expansion. For the which-path preparation, [F4] gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{\mathrm{mix}(w)}F_{a})=w\operatorname{tr}(\widehat\rho(\psi_{1})F_{a})+(1-w)\operatorname{tr}(\widehat\rho(\psi_{2})F_{a})$, and step 1.1 with $\psi=\psi_{j}$ gives the stated formula. This proves (a) and (b). [given, F2, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 [Loss] The completed family $(F_{a})_{a\in A}\cup\{F_{0}\}$ has nonnegative bounded effects summing to the identity by [F2], so [F1] gives $\nu(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})\ge0$, $\nu(0)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{0})\ge0$ and $\nu(0)+\sum_{a}\nu(a)=1$; hence $\nu(0)=1-\nu(A)$ and $\nu(A)\le1$, and if $\sum_{a}w_{a}=1$ almost everywhere then $F_{0}=0$ by [F2] and $\nu(0)=0$ for every preparation. Conversely assume $F_{0}\ne0$; then there is $x\in H_{s}$ with $F_{0}x\ne0$, and [F7] applied to the bounded positive operator $F_{0}$ gives $F_{0}^{1/2}x\ne0$ with $\langle F_{0}x,x\rangle=\|F_{0}^{1/2}x\|^{2}>0$; the pure preparation of the unit vector $\psi:=x/\|x\|$ then has $\nu(0)=\operatorname{tr}(\widehat\rho(\psi)F_{0})=\langle F_{0}\psi,\psi\rangle=\|x\|^{-2}\langle F_{0}x,x\rangle>0$ by step 1.1. This proves (c) up to conditioning. [given, F1, F2, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Conditioning] When $\nu(A)>0$, the recorded probabilities $\nu(a)$ of step 2.1 are nonnegative and sum to the positive number $\nu(A)$ by [F2], so dividing by $\nu(A)$ gives nonnegative numbers $\bar\nu(a)$ with $\sum_{a}\bar\nu(a)=1$; reading $\bar\nu$ as a set function on the finite set $A$ with its $\sigma$-algebra of all subsets, [F8] exhibits it as a probability measure on $A$. This completes (c). [given, step 2.1, F2, F8, algebra]

4.1 [Ideal bins and coincidence] For $w_{a}=\mathbf 1_{B_{a}}$ the effect is the position projection $F_{a}=G(B_{a})$ of the declared model, so $\nu(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho G(B_{a}))=\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B_{a})$ by [F6], the ideal bin probability. For the coincidence clause, multiply the almost-everywhere relation of the statement by $w_{a}$ and integrate: the weighted density $w_{a}[N\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle-c(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})]$ is integrable by [F5] and vanishes almost everywhere, so $N\int w_{a}\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle dx=c\int w_{a}(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})dx$ for every label; substituting into the formula of step 2.1 with $\varphi=0$ and into the formula of step 2.1 with $w=w_{*}$ gives $\nu_{\mathrm{coh}(0)}(a)=\nu_{\mathrm{mix}(w_{*})}(a)$ for every $a$, since $w_{*}\|\psi_{1}\|^{-2}=N^{-1}$. This proves (d), and (e) records the scope. [step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, F5, F6, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Where the response enters.** The recorded weights $w_{a}$ carry the declared
  finite resolution and efficiency of the model; the bin partition of the ideal
  detector is the special case of indicator weights. No value of any weight is
  asserted, and no apparatus realization is claimed.
- **Conditioning is not a state update.** The conditioned law is a statistical
  operation on the recorded sample; no claim is made about the post-detection
  state of the particle, and destructive or absorbing detection channels are
  outside the model's declared effects.

items.title: Continuity equation and local balance of the position probability of the massive model
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 with its internal-factor postulate P6, all
read through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $m>0$, a spin label $s$ with $r=2s+1$, nonempty
open sets $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, a
continuous real $V:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and a function
$\psi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb C^{r}$ whose components $\psi_{l}$ and the
functions $\partial_{t}\psi_{l}$, $\partial_{j}\psi_{l}$,
$\partial_{k}\partial_{j}\psi_{l}$ exist and are continuous on
$\Omega\times I$, and which satisfies the **model equation**
$$i\hbar\,\partial_{t}\psi_{l}(x,t)=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi_{l}(x,t)+V(x)\psi_{l}(x,t)\qquad(l=1,\dots,r,\ (x,t)\in\Omega\times I),$$
the componentwise reading of the Schroedinger equation of the model
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (a),
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (c)). Define the
**position density** and the **probability current** of the model by
$$n(x,t):=\|\psi(x,t)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2},\qquad j(x,t):=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}\bigl\langle\psi(x,t),\nabla\psi(x,t)\bigr\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}} =\frac{\hbar}{m}\sum_{l=1}^{r}\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{\psi_{l}(x,t)}\,\nabla\psi_{l}(x,t)\bigr).$$
Then:

(a) *Pointwise continuity.* For every $(x,t)\in\Omega\times I$,
$$\partial_{t}n(x,t)+\operatorname{div}j(x,t)=0 .$$

(b) *Integrated balance.* If $D\subseteq\Omega$ is a bounded open set with
$C^{1}$ boundary and $\overline D\subseteq\Omega$
([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-smooth-local-continuity-calculation]], in
which the divergence theorem for such domains is cited), then $t\mapsto\int_{D}n(x,t)dx$
is differentiable on $I$ with
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{D}n(x,t)\,dx=-\int_{\partial D}j(x,t)\cdot\nu(x)\,dS ,$$
$\nu$ the outward unit normal.

(c) *Global conservation under domination.* If $\Omega=\mathbb R^{3}$, if for
every $l$ there is $g_{l}\in L^{1}(\mathbb R^{3})$ with
$|\psi_{l}(x,t)|^{2}\le g_{l}(x)$ for almost every $x$ and every $t\in I$, and
if $\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{t\in I}\int_{\{|x|=R\}}|j_{l}(x,t)|\,dS=0$ for every
$l$, then $t\mapsto\sum_{l}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|\psi_{l}(x,t)|^{2}dx$ is
constant on $I$.

(d) *Flow conservation.* For the model's assigned unitary flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ on the model's state space and every
$\psi_{0}\in H_{s}$, one has $\|U(t)\psi_{0}\|=\|\psi_{0}\|$ for every
$t\in\mathbb R$; consequently the model's position probability of a unit
preparation integrates to one at every time, without the regularity hypotheses
of (a)-(c) ([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]] clause
(a)).

(e) *Units, reading and scope.* In the SI conventions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] the density $n$ has unit
$\mathrm m^{-3}$ and the current $j$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$;
the display of (a) is the local balance of the model's position probability in
its smooth regime, and (b) reads the rate of change of the probability of a
region as minus the outward probability flux across its boundary. The
statement does not assert that the flow of an arbitrary $L^{2}$ initial vector
has a representative obeying the regularity hypotheses of (a)-(c), does not
identify a recorded screen rate or any detection law with the surface flux (the
detection model of this page is the declared effect and bin model), and records
no empirical result.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The postulates and model readings of the statement; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; $m>0$, $r=2s+1$, open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ and interval $I$, continuous real $V$, the componentwise $C^{2}$ solution $\psi$ of the model equation, and the density $n$ and current $j$; in (d) a state vector $\psi_{0}\in H_{s}$ and the flow $U(t)$.

[F1] **Smooth scalar continuity theorem.** For $\hbar>0$, $m>0$, open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$, an open interval $I$, continuous real $V$ and a $C^{2}$ solution $u$ of $i\hbar\partial_{t}u=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta u+Vu$ on $\Omega\times I$ with continuous $\partial_{t}u$, the current $j_{u}:=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}(\overline u\nabla u)$ satisfies $\partial_{t}|u|^{2}+\operatorname{div}j_{u}=0$ pointwise and, on every bounded open $D$ with $C^{1}$ boundary and $\overline D\subseteq\Omega$, $\frac{d}{dt}\int_{D}|u|^{2}dx=-\int_{\partial D}j_{u}\cdot\nu\,dS$; moreover, if $\Omega=\mathbb R^{3}$, $|u(x,t)|^{2}\le g(x)$ for a.e. $x$ and every $t$ with $g\in L^{1}$, and $\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{t\in I}\int_{\{|x|=R\}}|j_{u}(x,t)|dS=0$, then $\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|u|^{2}dx$ is constant on $I$ ([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-smooth-local-continuity-calculation]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F2] **Componentwise model equation.** The model's scalar Hamiltonian is $H_{\mathrm{op}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta+V(Q)$ on the componentwise domain $W^{2,2}$, acting componentwise; its assigned flow is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$, and the Schroedinger equation holds in the norm-differentiable sense on the domain ([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (a), [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a)-(c), [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] clauses (i)-(iii), [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] clause (iv)).

[F3] **Flow conservation.** For the model's flow, $\|U(t)\psi_{0}\|=\|\psi_{0}\|$ for every $\psi_{0}\in H_{s}$ and every $t$, and the flow is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group ([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]] clause (a)).

[F4] **Units.** The position wave function of the model has unit $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$ in the position measure, so $n=|\psi|^{2}$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-3}$, the action $\hbar$ has unit $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$, the mass $m$ has unit $\mathrm{kg}$, and $\hbar/m$ has unit $\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$, so the current $j$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$ ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; apply the scalar continuity theorem to each component of the model equation, sum the componentwise identities and balances, sum the global conservation statements under the stated domination and flux hypotheses, and read flow conservation off the model's unitary group.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Componentwise continuity] For each $l$ the component $\psi_{l}$ satisfies the hypotheses of [F1] with the same $\Omega,I,V$ by [F2], so $\partial_{t}|\psi_{l}|^{2}+\operatorname{div}j_{l}=0$ pointwise with $j_{l}=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\psi_{l}}\nabla\psi_{l})$, and on every admissible $D$ one has $\frac{d}{dt}\int_{D}|\psi_{l}|^{2}dx=-\int_{\partial D}j_{l}\cdot\nu\,dS$. [given, F1, F2]

1.2 [Flow conservation] By [F3] applied to the model's flow, $\|U(t)\psi_{0}\|=\|\psi_{0}\|$ for every $\psi_{0}\in H_{s}$ and $t\in\mathbb R$; for a unit $\psi_{0}$ the total position probability is $\|U(t)\psi_{0}\|^{2}=1$ at every time. This proves (d). [given, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Summed local balance] Since $n=\sum_{l}|\psi_{l}|^{2}$, $j=\sum_{l}j_{l}$ and the sum is finite, adding the $r$ equations of step 1.1 gives $\partial_{t}n+\operatorname{div}j=\sum_{l}(\partial_{t}|\psi_{l}|^{2}+\operatorname{div}j_{l})=0$ pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, which is (a). For (b), finitely many differentiable functions may be added, so $t\mapsto\int_{D}n\,dx=\sum_{l}\int_{D}|\psi_{l}|^{2}dx$ is differentiable with derivative $-\sum_{l}\int_{\partial D}j_{l}\cdot\nu\,dS=-\int_{\partial D}j\cdot\nu\,dS$ by step 1.1 and linearity of the surface integral. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 [Global conservation] Assume the hypotheses of (c). Each component satisfies the domination hypothesis $|\psi_{l}|^{2}\le g_{l}$ and the flux hypothesis of [F1], so $\int|\psi_{l}|^{2}dx$ is constant on $I$ for every $l$; the finite sum $t\mapsto\sum_{l}\int|\psi_{l}|^{2}dx$ is then constant on $I$. This proves (c). [given, step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 [Conclusion] Steps 2.1, 2.2 and 1.2 establish (a)-(d); the unit computation of (e) reads the wave-function unit, the action unit and the mass unit of [F4]: $\hbar/m$ has unit $\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$, so $j$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$ while $n$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-3}$. The remaining assertions of (e) are scope statements: no regularity of the flow of an arbitrary $L^{2}$ vector is claimed, and no detection law is identified with the flux. [step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, F4, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **The smooth regime is an added hypothesis.** The theorem concerns a
  componentwise $C^{2}$ solution of the model equation. The model's assigned
  flow is norm-differentiable on its domain and conserves the total
  probability, but the existence of a $C^{2}$ representative with the stated
  pointwise equation is a separate regularity assumption and is not derived
  here.
- **The current is not a detection rate.** The current $j$ describes the local
  balance of the model's position probability; it is not by itself the
  recorded rate of a detector. The pair's recorded-outcome model assigns
  probabilities through the declared effects of the recorded detector.

The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited mathematics. It does not assert that the flow of an arbitrary L2 initial vector possesses a C2 representative, does not identify a screen record rate with the surface flux, and records no empirical result.

items.title: A finite sample can fail any nondegenerate fringe criterion with positive probability
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the declared two-path preparation model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] and the
declared recorded detector and sampling model
[[def-nrqm-interference-recorded-detector-and-sampling-model]] with finite
label set $A$, recorded law $\nu$ (a probability law on $A\cup\{0\}$, with $0$
the no-record label), and the declared $N$-trial sampling model of clause (d)
of that definition; the identification of repetitions with that model is the
additional statistical assumption of clause (ii) of the preparation and
apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).
Fix a preparation $\rho$, which may be a coherent preparation
$\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)$ or a which-path preparation
$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)$ of the declared model, so that its recorded law is the
law $\nu$ of [[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-recorded-bin-laws-loss-and-conditioning]]. Let
$(O_{1},\dots,O_{N})$ be the outcome sequence,
$S_{N}(a):=\#\{k:O_{k}=a\}$ and $F_{N}(a):=S_{N}(a)/N$ the empirical frequency
of $a\in A\cup\{0\}$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Concentration.* For every label $a$ and every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$\mathbb E\bigl[F_{N}(a)\bigr]=\nu(a),\qquad \operatorname{Var}\bigl(F_{N}(a)\bigr)=\frac{\nu(a)\bigl(1-\nu(a)\bigr)}{N},\qquad \mathbb P\bigl(|F_{N}(a)-\nu(a)|\ge\varepsilon\bigr)\le\frac{\nu(a)(1-\nu(a))}{N\varepsilon^{2}} .$$

(b) *Positive failure probability.* Let $C\subseteq(A\cup\{0\})^{N}$ be a
declared fringe criterion, and suppose there is a sequence
$(a_{1},\dots,a_{N})$ with $(a_{1},\dots,a_{N})\notin C$ and $\nu(a_{k})>0$ for
every $k$. Then the failure probability of the criterion is
$$\mathbb P\bigl((O_{1},\dots,O_{N})\notin C\bigr)\ge\prod_{k=1}^{N}\nu(a_{k})>0 .$$
In particular, if $\nu(a)>0$ for some label $a$, then every criterion that
rejects the constant sequence $(a,\dots,a)$ has failure probability at least
$\nu(a)^{N}>0$.

(c) *No discrimination between coincident laws.* If the recorded coherent law
of phase $0$ and the recorded which-path law of weight $w_{*}$ coincide in the
sense of clause (d) of
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-recorded-bin-laws-loss-and-conditioning]], then no
criterion whatsoever has different probability of acceptance under the two
declared preparations; in particular no finite sample distinguishes them with
certainty.

(d) *Scope.* Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional on the declared preparation,
detector and sampling models and the cited mathematics. The independence and
identical distribution of the trials are declared model assumptions, not
consequences of P1-P6; no failure probability, error rate, p-value, confidence
level, power, sample size or measured count is computed or asserted, and no
conclusion is drawn about any real apparatus. In particular the statements do
not assert that a coherent preparation must show a visible fringe pattern in a
finite sample, and do not assert that a sample without a visible pattern
falsifies the coherent model.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared preparation, detector and sampling models, with the recorded law $\nu$ on $A\cup\{0\}$; the outcome sequence $O_{1},\dots,O_{N}$ and the counts $S_{N}(a)$, $F_{N}(a)$; a declared criterion $C$ and a sequence $(a_{1},\dots,a_{N})$ as in (b); the Axiom of Countable Choice.

[F1] **Independent trials.** The random elements $O_{1},\dots,O_{N}$ are mutually independent and identically distributed with $\mathbb P(O_{k}=a)=\nu(a)$ for every $a\in A\cup\{0\}$ ([[def-nrqm-interference-recorded-detector-and-sampling-model]] clause (d), [[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]]); a binomial$(N,p)$ variable is a sum of $N$ mutually independent Bernoulli$(p)$ variables ([[def-bernoulli-and-binomial-random-variables]]).

[F2] **Finite-sampling law.** For $N\ge1$, independent $\{1,\dots,m\}$-valued variables with probabilities $p_{j}$, every sequence $(j_{1},\dots,j_{N})$ with all $p_{j_{k}}>0$ has probability $\prod_{k}p_{j_{k}}>0$, and every event disjoint from it has probability at most $1-\prod_{k}p_{j_{k}}<1$; for $N\ge1$ and a binomial$(N,p)$ variable $S$ the frequency $S/N$ has $\mathbb E[S/N]=p$, $\operatorname{Var}(S/N)=p(1-p)/N$ and $\mathbb P(|S/N-p|\ge\varepsilon)\le p(1-p)/(N\varepsilon^{2})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-chsh-and-finite-sampling-law]] clauses (b) and (c)).

[F3] **Recorded laws of the declared preparations.** The recorded probabilities of the coherent and which-path preparations are the laws of [[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]] clauses (a) and (b) as read by [[pthm-nrqm-interference-recorded-bin-laws-loss-and-conditioning]] clauses (a) and (b), and if the coincidence relation of the latter clause (d) holds then the recorded coherent law of phase $0$ and the recorded which-path law of weight $w_{*}$ agree on every label.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; identify the indicator variables of a fixed label as independent Bernoulli variables, apply the finite-sampling lemma for the concentration and positive-probability statements, and read the coincident-law statement off the declared laws.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Binomial marginals] Fix $a\in A\cup\{0\}$ and put $X_{k}:=\mathbf 1_{\{O_{k}=a\}}$. By [F1] the $X_{k}$ are mutually independent and identically distributed with $\mathbb P(X_{k}=1)=\nu(a)$ and $\mathbb P(X_{k}=0)=1-\nu(a)$, that is, Bernoulli$(\nu(a))$; hence $S_{N}(a)=\sum_{k=1}^{N}X_{k}$ is binomial$(N,\nu(a))$, and [F2] applied to $S=S_{N}(a)$ gives the three displayed formulas of (a). [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Positive-probability sequences] By mutual independence [F1], $\mathbb P(O_{k}=a_{k}\text{ for every }k)=\prod_{k}\nu(a_{k})$, a product of positive numbers; the failure event $\{(O_{1},\dots,O_{N})\notin C\}$ contains the complementary event of this outcome and is disjoint from it, so [F2] bounds its probability below by $\prod_{k}\nu(a_{k})$; the constant sequence is the special case. This proves (b). [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Conclusion] Under the coincidence hypothesis of (c), [F3] makes the two recorded laws equal as laws on $A\cup\{0\}$, so every event has the same probability under both preparations and no criterion has different acceptance probabilities; this proves (c). Together with steps 1.1 and 1.2 this establishes (a)-(c), and (d) records that the sampling model is a declared assumption and that no numerical failure probability, error rate or empirical conclusion is asserted. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, F2, F3, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **A null result is compatible with the coherent model.** By (b), for any
  criterion that would reject the outcome actually realized in some
  positive-probability sequence, failure has positive probability under the
  declared coherent model itself; a finite sample without a visible pattern is
  therefore not by itself a refutation.
- **A pattern is not a proof.** The same computation applies to the which-path
  model, and (c) shows that when the two recorded laws coincide no criterion
  distinguishes them. Agreement of a dataset with a declared model is
  evidence about the combined model, apparatus and sampling assumptions, not a
  proof of the model.

The item is a conditional consequence of the declared preparation and detector models, the declared sampling model in the sense of the preparation and apparatus postulate P7, and the cited mathematics. It asserts no measured counts, no p-value, no confidence level, no universal failure probability, and no empirical conclusion about nature; in particular, a finite sample without a visible fringe pattern is not a falsification of the coherent model, and a sample with a visible pattern is not a proof of it.

items.title: What the two-path detection page establishes, assumes and defers
items.statement:
## Scope of the page

**What is established.** The page declares the two-path preparation model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] with its
path components, coherent and which-path preparations and ideal detection bins,
and the recorded detector and sampling model
[[def-nrqm-interference-recorded-detector-and-sampling-model]] with its bounded
effects, no-record channel, loss conditioning and declared independent trials.
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]] derives the
normalized coherent bin law with its amplitude cross term, the which-path bin
law, and the criterion under which the two declared laws coincide on every bin.
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-recorded-bin-laws-loss-and-conditioning]] derives the
recorded-bin laws, the no-record mass and conditioned law, the reduction of
indicator weights to ideal bins, and a sufficient condition for the recorded
laws to coincide. [[pthm-nrqm-interference-continuity-and-local-probability-balance]]
derives the continuity equation and the local probability balance of the
model's smooth solutions and the norm conservation of the model's flow.
[[texp-nrqm-interference-finite-sample-fringe-failure]] shows that, within the
declared independent-trials model, a declared fringe criterion that rejects a
positive-probability outcome sequence fails with positive probability, and
that no criterion distinguishes two recorded laws that coincide.

**Adopted rather than derived.** The path components, the relative phase, the
preparation weight, the recorded weights and the independence of trials are
declarations of the preparation and apparatus models in the sense of P7; the
identification of a concrete arrangement with these declarations is a tested
identification with uncertainty and can fail. The appearance of an
interference pattern is not derived for any laboratory apparatus, and no
count, efficiency, resolution, background or calibration value appears on this
page.

**Not claimed.** The page does not assert which-path ontology, does not assign
a trajectory to the particle between preparation and detection, and does not
claim that the coherent preparation is the only admissible model of any
apparatus. It makes no claim that a lower-dimensional screen is a spatial
region of the model: a marginal, coarse-graining or flux reduction of a state
to a screen coordinate or surface is a separate detection model. It also makes
none of the following claims: that the flow of an arbitrary $L^{2}$ initial
vector has a $C^{2}$ representative; that a recorded screen rate equals the
surface flux; or that agreement of a finite dataset with a declared law
establishes the framework.

**Deferred content and destinations.** Visibility loss by path marking and
entanglement is not established here: the reusable marker-overlap physical
result is homed on the entanglement page
`qm-composites-entanglement-and-reduced-states`, and this page neither states
nor consumes it. Photon polarization and optical interference are out of scope
and belong to the photon and radiation page; the electron double-slit report is
reported on the companion examples page, not here. Comparative classical field
models and quantum-versus-classical model selection are likewise separate
models.

**Evidence status.** The page contains no experiment and no measured value;
the bounded, conditional statements above are consequences of the cited
postulates, declarations and mathematics. The companion examples page reports
one source-backed electron double-slit experiment with its disclosed
limitations, and that report tests the combined model and apparatus
assumptions rather than proving them.

items.title: An ideal flat two-path distribution: exact coherent and which-path bin laws
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the declared two-path preparation and detection model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] in its
spin-zero reading $r=1$, and the coherent and which-path detection laws
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]]. Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix lengths
$0<d<L<\infty$ and declare the two intervals
$$I_{1}:=\Bigl[-\frac d2-\frac L2,\ -\frac d2+\frac L2\Bigr],\qquad I_{2}:=\Bigl[\frac d2-\frac L2,\ \frac d2+\frac L2\Bigr]$$
on the first spatial coordinate, whose **overlap region**
$O:=I_{1}\cap I_{2}=[\frac d2-\frac L2,\ -\frac d2+\frac L2]$ has length
$L-d>0$; let $g\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{2})$ be a unit class and declare the
**flat path amplitudes**
$$f_{1}:=L^{-1/2}\mathbf 1_{I_{1}},\qquad f_{2}:=e^{i\varphi}L^{-1/2}\mathbf 1_{I_{2}}\qquad(\varphi\in\mathbb R),$$
with the declared path components
$$\psi_{j}(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}):=f_{j}(x_{1})\,g(x_{2},x_{3})\qquad(j=1,2).$$
A **slab bin** is a set $B_{1}\times\mathbb R^{2}$ with $B_{1}\subseteq\mathbb R$
Borel. Then:

(a) $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with
$\|\psi_{1}\|=\|\psi_{2}\|=1$, so the declared data are admissible, and the
model is admissible at every phase because $f_{1}+f_{2}\ne0$ on
$I_{1}\setminus I_{2}$.

(b) For every slab bin, with $N_{\varphi}:=\|f_{1}+f_{2}\|^{2}=2+\frac{2(L-d)}{L}\cos\varphi$,
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)}(B_{1}\times\mathbb R^{2})=\frac{1}{N_{\varphi}}\int_{B_{1}}|f_{1}+f_{2}|^{2}dx,\qquad \mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)}(B_{1}\times\mathbb R^{2})=\frac{w\,|B_{1}\cap I_{1}|+(1-w)\,|B_{1}\cap I_{2}|}{L}.$$

(c) The coherent density $|f_{1}+f_{2}|^{2}$ equals
$\frac{2(1+\cos\varphi)}{L}$ on $O$, equals $\frac1L$ on the symmetric
difference $I_{1}\triangle I_{2}$, and vanishes outside $I_{1}\cup I_{2}$;
consequently
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)}(O\times\mathbb R^{2})=\frac{(L-d)(1+\cos\varphi)}{L+(L-d)\cos\varphi},\qquad \mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)}\bigl((I_{j}\setminus I_{3-j})\times\mathbb R^{2}\bigr)=\frac{d}{2L+2(L-d)\cos\varphi}$$
for $j=1,2$, and for the balanced which-path preparation $w=\frac12$
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(1/2)}(O\times\mathbb R^{2})=\frac{L-d}{L},\qquad \mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(1/2)}\bigl((I_{j}\setminus I_{3-j})\times\mathbb R^{2}\bigr)=\frac{d}{2L}.$$

(d) At $\varphi=\pi$ the coherent law assigns probability zero to the whole
overlap region $O$ of positive length, while the balanced which-path law
assigns it probability $(L-d)/L>0$; every slab bin contained in $O$ has
coherent probability zero, every slab bin meeting $I_{1}\setminus I_{2}$ or
$I_{2}\setminus I_{1}$ in a set of positive length has positive coherent
probability, and every slab bin meeting $O$ in a set of positive length has
positive which-path probability.

The computation is exact in the declared model; it asserts no detector
response, no sampling model, no measured count and no laboratory realization.

## Verification

**Given:** The lengths $0<d<L<\infty$ and the intervals $I_{1},I_{2}$; the unit class $g$; the amplitudes $f_{1},f_{2}$ and components $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}$; a Borel set $B_{1}\subseteq\mathbb R$; phases $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ and weights $w\in[0,1]$; the Axiom of Countable Choice.

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the product-form norms by Tonelli, read the piecewise-constant densities and their integrals from the interval lengths, apply the declared laws to slab bins, and evaluate the overlap, outer and dark cases.

[L1] The model's coherent and which-path laws are $\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}}(B)=\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{-2}\int_{B}|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}|^{2}dx$ and $\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)}(B)=w\int_{B}|\psi_{1}|^{2}dx+(1-w)\int_{B}|\psi_{2}|^{2}dx$ for unit components ([[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]] clauses (a) and (b), [[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] clauses (c)-(e), [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] clause (ii)); the position density and the squared component norm agree almost everywhere ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).

[L2] Tonelli's theorem iterates integrals of nonnegative product-measurable functions over $\sigma$-finite products ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

[L3] A box in $\mathbb R^{n}$ is Lebesgue measurable of measure the product of its side lengths, for every choice of included faces ([[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]]); the integral of a nonnegative simple function is the finite sum of value times measure of its level set ([[def-integral-of-a-nonnegative-simple-function]]), and the integral is additive over disjoint measurable sets ([[cor-additivity-of-the-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]]).

1.1 [Product-form norms] For $j=1,2$, Tonelli and $\|g\|=1$, $\|f_{j}\|^{2}=|I_{j}|/L=1$ give $\|\psi_{j}\|^{2}=\int_{\mathbb R}\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|f_{j}(x_{1})|^{2}|g(x_{2},x_{3})|^{2}d(x_{2},x_{3})dx_{1}=\|f_{j}\|^{2}\|g\|^{2}=1\cdot1=1$, so $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}$ are nonzero unit classes. Since $f_{1}=L^{-1/2}$ on $I_{1}\setminus I_{2}$, a set of length $d>0$, one has $f_{1}+f_{2}\ne0$ for every $\varphi$. [given, L2, L3, algebra]

2.1 [Densities] On $O$ both indicators equal one, so $|f_{1}+f_{2}|^{2}=\frac{|1+e^{i\varphi}|^{2}}{L}=\frac{2(1+\cos\varphi)}{L}$; on $I_{1}\setminus I_{2}$ only $f_{1}$ contributes, giving $\frac1L$, and symmetrically on $I_{2}\setminus I_{1}$; outside $I_{1}\cup I_{2}$ both vanish. Integrating over $\mathbb R$ gives $\|f_{1}+f_{2}\|^{2}=\frac{2(1+\cos\varphi)(L-d)}{L}+\frac{2d}{L}=2+\frac{2(L-d)\cos\varphi}{L}=N_{\varphi}$, so the model is admissible at every phase. [step 1.1, L3, algebra]

3.1 [Slab laws] Write $\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}=(f_{1}+f_{2})g$ and $|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}|^{2}=|f_{1}+f_{2}|^{2}|g|^{2}$; Tonelli over $B_{1}\times\mathbb R^{2}$ gives $\int_{B_{1}\times\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}|^{2}d(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})=\bigl(\int_{B_{1}}|f_{1}+f_{2}|^{2}dx\bigr)\|g\|^{2}=\int_{B_{1}}|f_{1}+f_{2}|^{2}dx$, and likewise $\int_{B_{1}\times\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi_{j}|^{2}=\int_{B_{1}}|f_{j}|^{2}dx=|B_{1}\cap I_{j}|/L$; substituting into [L1] gives the two displayed laws of (b). [step 1.1, step 2.1, L1, L2, L3, algebra]

4.1 [Overlap, outer and dark values] Using the density values of step 2.1 and additivity of the integral, $\int_{O}|f_{1}+f_{2}|^{2}dx=\frac{2(1+\cos\varphi)(L-d)}{L}$ and $\int_{I_{j}\setminus I_{3-j}}|f_{1}+f_{2}|^{2}dx=\frac dL$, so the coherent values of (c) follow after dividing by $N_{\varphi}=2+\frac{2(L-d)\cos\varphi}{L}$: for the overlap, $\frac{2(1+\cos\varphi)(L-d)/L}{2(L+(L-d)\cos\varphi)/L}=\frac{(L-d)(1+\cos\varphi)}{L+(L-d)\cos\varphi}$, and for each outer region $\frac{d/L}{2(L+(L-d)\cos\varphi)/L}=\frac{d}{2L+2(L-d)\cos\varphi}$; the two outer values and the overlap value sum to one. The which-path values follow from $|B_{1}\cap I_{j}|/L$ with $w=\frac12$ and $|O|=L-d$, $|I_{j}\setminus I_{3-j}|=d$. At $\varphi=\pi$ the coherent overlap value is zero, the outer values are $d/(2L-2(L-d))=\frac12$ each, and the which-path overlap value is $\frac{L-d}{L}>0$ because $L>d$; a bin contained in $O$ has $|B_{1}\cap I_{1}|=|B_{1}\cap I_{2}|=|B_{1}|$ and coherent density zero there, while a bin meeting an outer region in a set of positive length meets $\{f_{1}+f_{2}\ne0\}$ in a set of positive length, so its coherent probability is positive; the which-path positivity for bins meeting $O$ follows from $\frac12|B_{1}\cap I_{1}|/L>0$. This proves (c) and (d). [step 3.1, L3, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **The dark region is a feature of the declared flat model.** The vanishing of
  the coherent density on all of $O$ at $\varphi=\pi$ uses the flat amplitudes
  and the exact cancellation $f_{1}+f_{2}=0$ there; a model with unequal
  weights or non-flat amplitudes need not vanish on a region. A slab bin that
  contains part of $O$ and part of an outer region still has positive coherent
  probability, and no recorded event is forbidden by the vanishing density on
  $O$ unless the bin lies inside $O$.
- **No data are used.** The example computes probabilities in the declared
  model; it does not report counts, and the flat amplitudes are a declared
  idealization, not a measured profile.
