items.title: A declared finite phase-averaging model reproduces the which-path law for orthogonal components
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the declared two-path preparation and detection model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] with path
components $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\ne0$ satisfying
$\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$ (orthogonal components), and the coherent
and which-path detection laws
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]]. Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix an integer $n\ge2$
and declare the **finite phase-averaging model**: the relative phase takes the
$n$ values
$$\varphi_{k}:=\frac{2\pi k}{n}\qquad(k=0,1,\dots,n-1)$$
with equal statistical weight $1/n$, so that the averaged bin law of a Borel
set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ is
$$\bar p(B):=\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi_{k})}(B).$$
Put $N:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}$ and $w_{*}:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}/N$.
Then:

(a) $\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi_{k}}\psi_{2}\|^{2}=N$ for every $k$, so every
coherent preparation of the declared model has the same normalization $N$;

(b) the averaged cross term vanishes bin by bin:
$$\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}2\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(e^{-i\varphi_{k}}\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx\Bigr)=0 ;$$

(c) consequently $\bar p(B)=\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w_{*})}(B)$ for every
Borel set $B$: the declared finite phase-averaging model reproduces the
which-path law with the norm weights, while each single phase shows the cross
term of [[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]].

The averaging over the phase is a declared statistical model of the preparation
ensemble in the sense of clause (ii) of the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]; the computation asserts no
decoherence mechanism, no detector response, no counts and no empirical result,
and it does not cover the continuous uniform phase distribution, which would
require its own integral model.

## Verification

**Given:** The declared model data with $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\ne0$, $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$; an integer $n\ge2$ with phases $\varphi_{k}=2\pi k/n$; a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$; $N=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}$ and $w_{*}=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}/N$; the Axiom of Countable Choice.

[L1] The coherent and which-path laws are $\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)}(B)=\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{-2}\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}dx$ and $\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)}(B)=w\|\psi_{1}\|^{-2}\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}dx+(1-w)\|\psi_{2}\|^{-2}\int_{B}\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}dx$, and the coherent numerator expands as $\int_{B}(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})dx+2\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle dx)$ ([[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]] clauses (a) and (b), [[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] clauses (c)-(e)).

[L2] The $n$-th roots of unity are $e^{i2\pi k/n}$ for $k=0,\dots,n-1$ ([[thm-complex-nth-roots-and-roots-of-unity]], [[def-complex-exponential]]), and for $n\ge2$ their sum is zero ([[cor-sum-of-roots-of-unity]]).

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the coherent norm under orthogonality, average the cross term over the roots of unity, and read the averaged law off the coherent and which-path formulas.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [L1]-[L2].

1.1 [Phase-independent normalization] For every $k$, [L1] gives $\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi_{k}}\psi_{2}\|^{2}=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}+2\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1},e^{i\varphi_{k}}\psi_{2}\rangle=N+2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e^{-i\varphi_{k}}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle\bigr)=N$, since $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$. This proves (a). [given, L1, algebra]

1.2 [Root sum] The numbers $e^{i\varphi_{k}}$, $k=0,\dots,n-1$, are exactly the $n$-th roots of unity and $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^{-1}$ permutes them, so $\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}e^{-i\varphi_{k}}=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}e^{i\varphi_{k}}=0$ by [L2]. [given, L2, algebra]

2.1 [Averaged law] By step 1.1 each summand of $\bar p(B)$ has denominator $N$, and by [L1] its numerator is $\int_{B}(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})dx+2\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi_{k}}\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle dx)$. Averaging the $n$ summands and using linearity of the finite average, the cross term contributes $\frac{2}{N}\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\bigl(\frac1n\sum_{k}e^{-i\varphi_{k}}\bigr)\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle dx\bigr)=0$ by step 1.2, and the remaining term is $\frac1N\int_{B}(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})dx=w_{*}\frac{\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}dx}{\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}}+(1-w_{*})\frac{\int_{B}\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}dx}{\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}}$, since $w_{*}\|\psi_{1}\|^{-2}=N^{-1}=(1-w_{*})\|\psi_{2}\|^{-2}$; this is $\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w_{*})}(B)$ by [L1]. This proves (b) and (c). [step 1.1, step 1.2, L1, L2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **The averaging is not a dynamics.** Nothing here evolves the state or removes
  coherence dynamically; the computation concerns a declared ensemble of
  preparations whose relative phase is randomized over a finite set. A
  continuous uniform phase distribution is a different declared model and is
  not computed here.
- **Orthogonality is used.** The identification of the averaged law with the
  which-path law uses $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$, which makes the
  normalization independent of the phase. For non-orthogonal components the
  averaged law need not coincide with the which-path law, and no claim is made
  about that case.

The example is a conditional computation in the declared model; it asserts no decoherence mechanism, no environmental model, no detector response, no counts and no empirical result, and it does not cover the continuous uniform phase distribution.

items.title: Reported controlled double-slit electron diffraction with single-electron detection (Bach, Pope, Liou and Batelaan)
items.statement:
## Setup

The source is the primary preprint of Bach, Pope, Liou and Batelaan
(arXiv:1210.6243v1, 22 October 2012), reporting a controlled double-slit
electron diffraction experiment. The reported apparatus consists of a
thermionic tungsten filament with electrostatic lenses producing an electron
beam of energy 600 eV; a collimation aperture of 2 micrometre width and
10 micrometre height placed 16.5 cm from the source; a double-slit 30.5 cm
beyond the collimation aperture, milled with a 30 keV Ga+ focused-ion-beam
system into a 100 nm silicon-nitride membrane coated with about 2 nm of gold,
with two slits of 50 nm width, 280 nm centre-to-centre separation and
4 micrometre height, each with a 150 nm support midway; a movable mask
5 micrometre wide, driven by a piezoelectric actuator and placed 230 micrometre
downstream of the double-slit; an electrostatic quadrupole lens magnifying the
pattern; and a two-dimensional microchannel plate and phosphor screen imaged by
a CCD camera. The body of the paper gives the mask height as 10 micrometre
while the caption of figure 1 gives 20 micrometre; the inconsistency is
recorded and not resolved here. The comparison is a reported experiment of the
framework in the sense of the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]; the identification of the
reported device with the quantities of any model's preparation or detection is
an apparatus identification carrying the source's limitations.

## Procedure

Two procedures are reported. First, for the slit-control measurements the mask
is moved across the double-slit so that predominantly one slit, then both
slits, then the other slit transmit; the recorded image frames for each mask
position are summed and the accumulated image normalized, producing the
distributions labelled P1 (slit 1), P12 (both slits) and P2 (slit 2). Second,
for the build-up measurement the mask is centred, the source intensity is
reduced until the detection rate in the pattern is about 1 Hz, the quadrupole
lens is set to magnify the central five diffraction orders, and localized
detections are recorded with a blob-localization scheme; the reported final
accumulation took about 2 hours. The paper reports an average distance between
consecutive electrons of 2.3e6 m at this rate and energy, and states that this
ensures at most one electron is present in the 1 m apparatus at any time. No
arrival-process law, occupancy bound, event-selection rule, dead-time model or
independence test is reported, so that statement remains a reported
apparatus-behaviour inference; the finite-sampling mathematics that a declared
independent-trials analysis would require is available in
[[lem-nrqm-composites-chsh-and-finite-sampling-law]], but no such analysis is
performed here or in the source.

## Observations

The paper reports, and the retained figures show, slit-selective probability
distributions: a single-slit central diffraction order in the P1 and P2
configurations and a double-slit distribution in the P12 configuration, with
weak double-slit contributions visible in the first diffraction order of the
nominal single-slit configurations, which the paper attributes to the finite
separation between the mask and the double-slit. For the mask-centred build-up
the figure captions report accumulated localized-event counts of 2, 7, 209,
1004 and 6235 in five successive images of the central five orders, the paper
describing the earliest images as appearing random and a pattern becoming
discernible at the largest counts, with a clearly visible pattern in the final
image. Each reported detection is a localized blob whose size represents the
localization error of the detection scheme; the accumulated distribution, not
any single event, carries the reported pattern.

## Uncertainty

The report supplies no numerical uncertainty budget for its observations. In
detail: no calibrated detector efficiency or background map is given; no
numerical value of the localization error is given although the blob size is
said to represent it; no uncertainty is given for the beam energy, the slit
dimensions or the mask position; no statistical independence of the recorded
events is tested; no event-selection or image-processing error rate is
quantified; and no significance level, confidence interval or fitted
comparison with a competing distribution is reported. The mask-height
inconsistency between the body text and the figure caption is unresolved. The
reported claim that at most one electron is present at a time rests on the
average-separation estimate and not on a bound on the probability of two
electrons in the apparatus. The approximate rate of about 1 Hz and duration of
about 2 hours are not converted here into a trial count, efficiency or
calibrated rate, and no uncertainty is manufactured for them.

## Interpretation

The source interprets the slit-selective patterns and the build-up of a
diffraction pattern from localized detections as a realization of Feynman's
two-slit thought experiment, illustrating interference and wave-particle
duality for electrons. Read as a report, the accumulated distributions and
their dependence on which slits transmit are consistent with a coherent
electron-amplitude model under the reported preparation and apparatus
conditions; the report's own comparison is qualitative and no competing
incoherent or classical model is specified, fitted or tested, so the report
does not by itself discriminate between such models. Classical wave models
also exhibit interference, so a reported pattern does not establish the
quantum framework or exclude every alternative; conversely, nothing here
falsifies a model, and each recorded event remains a localized detection whose
relation to any theoretical amplitude is a model identification. A controlled
test of the declared two-path law
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]] would require a
declared preparation model, a declared detector response including efficiency,
resolution and background, a declared competing law, and a declared sampling
model with its statistical method; none of these is supplied by this report,
and no such analysis is performed here. Agreement of the reported
distributions with a model would be evidence about the combined model,
apparatus and analysis assumptions, not a proof of the model.

empirical_result.uncertainty: The report supplies no numerical uncertainty budget: no calibrated detector efficiency or background map, no numerical localization standard deviation (the blob size is said to represent the localization error, without a value), no arrival-process law or test of mutual independence of detections, no event-selection error rate, no statistical significance, confidence interval or fitted competing-model comparison, and no uncertainty on beam energy, slit dimensions or mask position. A source inconsistency in the mask height (5 micrometre by 10 micrometre in the body versus 5 micrometre by 20 micrometre in the figure 1 caption) is unresolved. The statements that at most one electron is present and that electron-electron interactions are eliminated rest on an average-separation estimate (2.3e6 m) rather than on a bound on two-electron occupancy. These are reported specifications and settings, not independently recalibrated measurements.

items.title: What the worked items and the reported experiment of the examples page establish
items.statement:
## Scope of the examples page

**The two computations.** [[ex-nrqm-interference-ideal-flat-two-path-screen-distribution]]
computes, in the declared two-path model with flat product-form amplitudes, the
exact coherent and which-path probabilities of the overlap and outer regions of
the declared detection coordinate: at relative phase $\pi$ the coherent law
assigns probability zero to the whole overlap region while the balanced
which-path law assigns it positive probability, and a bin meeting a bright
region has positive coherent probability. [[ex-nrqm-interference-uniform-phase-averaging]]
shows that for orthogonal path components a declared ensemble whose relative
phase is uniformly distributed over the finitely many $n$-th roots of unity has
the which-path law with the norm weights as its averaged law. Both are
conditional computations in the declared model under the pair's detection laws
([[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]]); neither is a
dynamics, an environmental decoherence model, a detector response or a
statement about an apparatus.

**The reported experiment.** [[exp-nrqm-interference-bach-electron-double-slit]]
reports the primary preprint of Bach, Pope, Liou and Batelaan: a 600 eV
electron beam through a nanofabricated double-slit with slit-selective
distributions and a single-electron event build-up over 2, 7, 209, 1004 and
6235 accumulated localized events. The report supplies no calibrated
efficiency or background, no numerical localization error, no uncertainty for
its apparatus parameters, no occupancy bound and no statistical comparison
with a specified competing model; the mask-height inconsistency between its
body and its figure caption is recorded as unresolved. The item therefore
supports a qualitative operational account only, and its agreement with any
model is evidence about the combined model and apparatus assumptions, not a
proof of the framework, not a demonstration that every event is independent,
and not a demonstration that only one electron is in the apparatus at a time.

**What the page does not address.** No photon experiment is reported here; a
single-photon polarization or counting experiment belongs to the photon and
radiation page, and the classical wave comparison for light is a separate
declared model. No experiment testing the which-path or marker variants of the
arrangement is reported. No claim is made that the finite sample of the
reported experiment would distinguish the coherent from the which-path
recorded law; [[texp-nrqm-interference-finite-sample-fringe-failure]] shows
that both can fail or pass a finite-sample criterion and that coincident
recorded laws are indistinguishable by any criterion.

**Evidence status.** The page combines exact conditional computations with one
faithfully reported experiment. It contains no simulation presented as data,
no invented count, precision or significance, and no conclusion about nature;
the empirical qualifications of the report are carried in its Observations and
Uncertainty sections and are not strengthened here.
